newsitem.title: BULGARIA: BULGARIA ISSUE DEPT ASSETS UP 42 MLN MARKS IN WEEK.
newsitem.headline: BULGARIA ISSUE DEPT ASSETS UP 42 MLN MARKS IN WEEK.

text.p: The Bulgarian National Bank (BNB) Issue Department foreign exchange assets rose to the lev equivalent of 3.529 billion marks on August 8 from 3.487 billion marks a week earlier, BNB figures showed on Monday.
BNB officials declined comment on the reasons for the rise.

Under an IMF-prescribed currency board regime introduced on July 1 the lev was pegged at 1,000 per mark as an anchor currency and the BNB pledged to buy and sell unlimited volumes of marks at 995 levs bid and 1,000 ask.

The currency board bans the BNB from lending to the government and commercial banks and requires levs in circulation to be fully matched by the Issue Department's assets, which make up the BNB foreign exchange reserves.
The cash and nostro accounts in foreign currencies fell to the lev equivalent of 1.520 billion marks on August 8 from 1.721 billion marks on August 1, figures showed.
BNB holdings in foreign securities rose to 1.360 trillion levs from 1.118 trillion levs.

Apart from holdings in foreign securities and cash and nostro accounts in foreign currency, the Issue Department assets included 640.7 billion levs in monetary gold and eight billion levs in accrued interest receivable as of August 8.
Any rise in the Issue Department assets allows for a limited rise of the lev currency in circulation without accumulating inflationary pressure under the currency board.
The mark fall against the dollar on global markets last week boosted the lev price of the Issue Department foreign exchange assets, because they are mostly held in dollar-denominated instruments.
Under the BNB law the market value of the assets, denominated in foreign currency other than the mark has been limited to two percent of the total BNB liabilities denominated in the same currency.
So far there are no official figures on BNB operations to transfer part of dollar reserves into mark-denominated assets.
Currency in circulation, part of the Issue Department liabilities, rose to 882.2 billion levs on August 8 from 832.8 billion levs on August 1.
The department's liabilities also included 696.5 billion levs in bank deposits and current accounts on August 8, down from 698.3 billion levs a week earlier.
Since July 14, when the BNB halted interest payments on banks' current accounts at the BNB, local banks have pared their holdings in those accounts.
The State Fund for Reconstuction and Development account, also part of the department's liabilities, rose to 628.6 billion levs on August 8 from 609 billion levs on August 1.
Government deposits and accounts, a liability of the Issue Department, fell to 503.1 billion levs on August 8 from 540.3 billion levs a week earlier.
The liabilities also included a 803.7 billion lev deposit of the BNB Banking Department on August 8, a rise by 15.2 billion levs from August 1.

Under the currency board system the Banking Department is the lender of last resort for local commercial banks. It can extend refinancing to sound banks only in case of systemic risk for the banking and payments system. -- Sofia Newsroom +359-2 981 4145
